# Course Information & Logistics {.unnumbered}

This page holds the rules of the course: what you need to do to pass, how the grade is set, and who to contact.

## Exam and requirements

The course has three mandatory parts:

- **The labs** are pass/fail, and must all be passed to pass the course (see [Labs](#labs) below). If you pass **every** lab quiz by its due date (see [Labs](#labs)), you get 5 extra points on the exam; a single late lab means no extra points.
- **The project** is graded 0-100, and you need at least 40% to pass it. It has three graded parts: the code you have written, the final report, and an oral presentation of your code to one of the teaching assistants. See the [Capstone](capstone.qmd) page for the task and the grading criteria.
- **The exam** is a pen-and-paper exam, graded 0-100; you need at least 40% to pass it. You may bring up to five pages (single-sided) of your own notes.

The final grade is 70% from the exam and 30% from the project, and you need 50% in total to pass. The grade scale (not exactly the default one at SU) is:

| Grade | A | B | C | D | E | Fx | F |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total score | ≥ 90% | ≥ 80% | ≥ 70% | ≥ 60% | ≥ 50% | ≥ 45% | < 45% |

The 5 extra points for passing all labs on time count only on the main exam, not on a re-exam, and only once. If you fail the exam, a re-exam is normally offered a few weeks after the course; if you have already passed (grade E or higher), there is no retake to improve the grade. Past exams are on the [Schedule](schedule.qmd#exam-preparation) page. Two question-and-answer sessions, one after Session 6 and one after Session 12, are there to ask about anything in the course before the exam; bring your questions.

## Labs {#labs}

Most sessions have a lab (see the [Course Schedule](schedule.qmd)): a notebook in this book, with a short online quiz on Canvas.

- **Mandatory.** Every lab quiz must be passed, with at least 50% correct.
- **Due before the next lecture.** Each lab quiz is due at 23:59 the evening before the next lecture (the last one the evening before the exam; when the next lecture is the morning after the lab, you get one more day), so that you come to each lecture with the previous lab done; the dates are on Canvas.
- **Available as soon as published.** You do not have to wait for the lecture.
- **One redo chance** if you fail, normally only the next time the course runs, and the lab may have changed by then.

## Expected workload {#workload}

The course is full time for four weeks and two days: about 176 hours of work, at eight hours a day. The table below gives our estimate of where that time goes: each session has its lecture (three hours; Sessions 0 and 1 share one), reading the material and doing the lab, and then come the capstone project and the exam.

- **Reading and understanding** means studying the session page carefully, with its worked examples, practice problems, quiz and main videos, and working through the course notebook. Optional videos and boxes are not included.
- **Lab** is the total time for the lab, including its quiz on Canvas. Every lab is designed to fit into the scheduled three-hour lab afternoon, and most students need about two to two and a half hours. Optional extras in the lab notebooks are not included.

| Part of the course | Lecture | Reading and understanding | Lab | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 Introduction | 1 h | 0.5 h | – | 1.5 h |
| 1 Mathematics | 2 h | 7.5 h | no lab | 9.5 h |
| Setup, before Session 2 | – | – | 0.5 h | 0.5 h |
| 2 Python | 3 h | 4.5 h | 2.5 h | 10 h |
| 3 Biological databases | 3 h | 2.5 h | 2 h | 7.5 h |
| 4 Sequence alignment | 3 h | 3 h | 2.5 h | 8.5 h |
| 5 Database search and profiles | 3 h | 3 h | 2.5 h | 8.5 h |
| 6 Protein structure | 3 h | 2.5 h | 2.5 h | 8 h |
| 7 Linear models and XOR | 3 h | 4.5 h | 1.5 h | 9 h |
| 8 Machine-learning foundations | 3 h | 4.5 h | 2 h | 9.5 h |
| 9 Training neural networks | 3 h | 4.5 h | 2 h | 9.5 h |
| 10 CNNs | 3 h | 3.5 h | 2.5 h | 9 h |
| 11 Sequences and language models | 3 h | 4.5 h | 2.5 h | 10 h |
| 12 AlphaFold | 3 h | 5 h | 2.5 h | 10.5 h |
| **All sessions** | **36 h** | **50 h** | **25.5 h** | **111.5 h** |
| Capstone project: introduction, help session, your own work, report and oral presentation | | | | 40 h |
| Exam preparation, including the Q&A sessions | | | | 20 h |
| Written exam | | | | 4 h |
| **Whole course** | | | | **175.5 h** |

These numbers are estimates from the amount of material, not measurements, and they depend a lot on your background. If you already know Python well, Session 2 goes quickly, and if the mathematics is new to you, Session 1 takes longer. The sessions take about 110 hours with the lectures, and the [capstone project](capstone.qmd) and the exam about 65 hours together.

## Plagiarism

Plagiarism has unfortunately been an issue in earlier years. You may already have signed a plagiarism policy form; if not, you will be given one. Please set an example of honesty for your peers, since not everyone has fully understood the rules. If you see a problem, or have a suggestion for how to handle it, talk to the teachers. In general we trust everyone: you are honest until proven otherwise.

Plagiarism is copying the work of others, whether from online or printed sources, your peers, or anyone else, without attributing it directly and explicitly. Discussing methods and approaches with other students is encouraged; submitting someone else's answers, code or text as your own is not.

- All written reports are checked for plagiarism.
- Plagiarism can lead to suspension from the university.

If you are unsure where the line is on a specific assignment, ask before you submit, not after.

## AI tools

You may use AI tools during the course, but not during the exam. The final report and the labs must not be written by AI tools, but you may use them as a "science buddy", for example to understand a method or to improve your report. Session 2's "How to use chatbots" section shows how to use them well.

## Schedule

The schedule is on Canvas. As far as possible, teaching is on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, with lectures 09:00-12:00 and labs 13:00-16:00. What each session covers is on the [Course Schedule](schedule.qmd) page.
